lines: A fair chance can look a lot like standing around until the right bell rings.
I once followed the bell hoping it meant opportunity. It meant <jump>hurry</jump>.
I organized a barrel once. For a moment, everyone thought I had a calling.
There is a story from the village square, but it sounds smaller unless you were standing there.
Most stories here begin with someone saying, 'It will only take a moment.' They are always wrong.
I remember the smell of rain, the sound of the bell, and everyone suddenly pretending they had a plan.
The funny part came later. At the time, nobody was laughing.
A village story changes depending on who got embarrassed in it.
I could make it grand, but honestly, it was mostly mud, noise, and bad timing.
Still, we tell it because we made it through, and that makes people stand a little straighter.
Once I helped three different workers and got paid in advice from all of them.
A job site opened up for one morning and somehow everyone had an opinion about my future.
I carried bricks, bread, and gossip in the same day. Only one spilled.
A child asked what my job was and I said looking available. They accepted it.
I once fixed a fence by standing nearby while the right person explained loudly.
During a raid, nobody asked about my profession before handing me supplies.
A trader called me flexible and meant cheap. I smiled anyway.
I spent a week trying trades in my head and ended up very tired.
One morning every workstation was taken and every chore found me instead.
I once sorted seeds so neatly the farmer looked worried.
A barrel fell over and I became an expert in picking things up.
The bell rang while I was carrying soup. Heroism became very slippery.
I learned more from sweeping near a smith than from asking foolish questions.
A villager told me to find my calling. I found their missing bucket first.
There was a day when being unassigned meant being exactly where I was needed.
